items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: You had Marshall Royal was our musical director.

ctx.x: In your head, were you thinking it’s this or perhaps the infantry?

Oh yeah. We were all thinking that. Everybody was thinking out there in the mud in the trenches. We were all thinking that. And also this was a chance, I was pretty raw, very raw as a musician. I had only been in the local, I joined in ’37 so I’d been in the local five years, and my experience — I was kind of limited. I had done little dance jobs playing with small groups. But we’ll probably get around to that as we go through my musical history. So I jumped at the chance. And it was a Godsend because in that…

lead alto players in the country. His brother, Ernie Royal, outstanding trumpet player who ended up in New York doing studio work, but they all were with the original Lionel Hampton band, the band that made “Flying Home.” Vernon Alley of course, Mister Music, he was in the band, Wilbert Baranco, who is mentioned in the Leonard Feather, who was a very fine musician/pianist/singer and arranger. Wilbert, during the WPA days, he had been connected with the music project in San Francisco, and he wrote for everything,…

items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: The drummer is San Franciscan. He's a business agent for the San Francisco local and his name is Earl Watkins.

ctx.x: The leader is standing there, right?

No, there's another fellow that is not seen. I'll recall his name in a minute. Then the trombone player in the middle is Ralph Bledsoe (PHONETIC) who at the present time is one of our better known physicians in town. He's a urologist. He's flanked on both sides by two trombone players, both of them -- one of them, his name is Dan Hamilton. The drummer is San Franciscan. He's a business agent for the San Francisco local and his name is Earl Watkins. The first trumpet player there next to him is my kid brother,…
old Kansas City trumpet players, Herman Grimes. The other trumpet player is one of a set of twins, the Gregory twins. I'm on the end over there somewhere.
